matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old handler attempted a live GitHub fetch on every GET request and fell back to the database only on failure. The new handler unconditionally serves from the database, removing the GitHub call entirely. A deployed caller that does not change anything now receives stale data instead of the fresh data it previously got. This is a behavioral breaking change to the contract.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id response shape narrowed — undocumented GitHub fields removed

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response shape narrowed — undocumented GitHub fields removed
findings.rationale: The old GET handler returned `{ ...detail, id: pr.id }` where `detail` was the full GitHub PR response (including fields like `head`, `base`, `labels`, `milestone`, `assignees`, etc.). The new handler returns only a fixed set of fields (id, number, title, author, branch, base, head_sha, additions, deletions, files_count, status, opened_at, updated_at, body, files, commits). Any caller that relied on undocumented fields from the GitHub response will silently lose data. The web client is updated in this PR and uses only the documented fields, so it is not affected. External callers or future consumers that depended on the extra fields will break. The compatible alternative is to either keep the old behavior for a transition period or document the full response shape and ensure the new POST /pulls/:id/refresh returns the same shape as the old GET.

The new handler returns only a fixed subset of fields (id, number, title, author, branch, base, head_sha, additions, deletions, files_count, status, opened_at, updated_at, body, files, commits). Any caller that reads a field that was previously present in the GitHub response but is now omitted will receive `undefined`, which can cause silent breakage (e.g. a UI that shows a mergeable badge, an e2e test that asserts on labels, or an external consumer that processes review data). The new `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` endpoint does return the full GitHub payload, but it is a different route and method, so existing callers of GET are not automatically migrated.
